what_this_is: The answer key for the claim-integrity check. Thirteen real findings from the previous sprint's round 5, each labelled with the class that reaches it and the bucket it scores in. Labelled BEFORE the check was designed, so the key cannot be tuned to fit the check. Changing any bucket costs a work-doc entry naming which finding moved and why (AC1b).

field_guide.id: The finding's id in the archived round 5 record.
field_guide.severity_as_filed: What the reviewer filed it as, before the refuter ruled.
field_guide.refuter_verdict_verbatim: The refutation table cell, as written.
field_guide.refuted_on: scope, fact, or null. A finding refuted on SCOPE is still a true statement about the tree, so a class may reach it. A finding refuted on FACT is not, so no class may claim it.
field_guide.citation: file:line into the archived work-doc where the finding is described.
field_guide.verdict_citation: file:line of the finding's row in the round 5 refutation and decision table.
field_guide.reaching_class: Exactly one candidate class, or none.
field_guide.bucket: must_catch when a class reaches it AND the scope permits. out_of_class otherwise.
field_guide.block_reason: For out_of_class only. no_class_reaches when no candidate class names the shape at all. scope_blocked when a class names the shape but scope or the annotation requirement stops it. refuted_on_fact when claiming it would reproduce a false claim.
field_guide.why: One sentence. For out_of_class it names the property that blocks it.
field_guide.replay: Where the finding can be scored from. live_at_head, class_live_via_siblings, requires_fixture, or n_a_behavioural.
field_guide.replay_note: What a scorer must do to score this finding.
field_guide.claiming_is_defect: Present and true only where the check reporting this finding as caught would be a DEFECT rather than a point.

candidate_classes.C1_annotated_count: A count in prose that no longer matches. Requires an annotation the claim does not currently carry, and is diff-scoped, so a pre-existing unannotated count in a file no diff touches is not reachable.
candidate_classes.C2_citation_resolves: A file.ext:N that does not resolve. Repo-wide.
candidate_classes.C3_declared_vs_used: A {{token}} used in an agent prompt but absent from its INPUTS list. Repo-wide.
candidate_classes.C4_check_exists: A check [NN] reference naming no real check, or a claim that something is pinned or enforced that points at a comment rather than executable code. Repo-wide.
candidate_classes.C5_retired_vocabulary: A retired name surviving in a live file. Repo-wide, allowlisted.
candidate_classes.C6_section_exists: A doc telling a writer to use a work-doc section the template does not have. Repo-wide.
candidate_classes.C7_literal_absent_claim: A sentence whose truth is decidable by looking for a literal, asserted in either direction: claiming a phrase is absent, unpinned or not present where it IS present, or claiming a phrase is present, named, wired or covered where it is NOT. Repo-wide. Widened to both polarities by decision #13-A after this table was frozen; the one-directional text it replaces is preserved in notes entry n9.

replay_states.live_at_head: The filed site still carries the false claim at the derived_at commit. Scoreable by running the check over the tree as it stands.
replay_states.class_live_via_siblings: The filed site was fixed, but out-of-file siblings of the same class are live at the derived_at commit. A sibling hit is NOT the filed site, and scoring it as the filed finding is a judgement the scorer must make deliberately.
replay_states.requires_fixture: The filed site was fixed or corrected after the finding landed. Scoring needs the historical blob or a fixture reproducing it. This is what T1b's fixtures half exists for.
replay_states.n_a_behavioural: No textual site to replay. The finding is about runtime behaviour or about what a record fails to contain.

findings.one_line: The per-literal loop walks the tree once per banned literal, 8 git grep invocations on the pre-commit path where a batched screen needs 2.
findings.why: It is a runtime cost property of shell code measured by timing invocations, and no doc asserts anything about it, so there is no claim for any class to falsify.
findings.replay_note: Nothing textual to replay. The finding was proven by timing 20 iterations over 248 tracked files.

findings.one_line: implement-and-test.md:34 tells a writer to append an entry to the Implementation Log, a work-doc section the template retired in favour of Daily Updates.
findings.why: It is exactly a doc instructing a writer to use a work-doc section the template does not have, and C6 is repo-wide so no diff scope blocks it.
findings.replay_note: The filed site was fixed at ab5cb74. Three sibling instruction-sites are live at the derived_at commit: debug-when-stuck.md:19, debug-when-stuck.md:190, README.md:416. Scoring a sibling as the filed finding is a deliberate call, not an accident, and it must be written down when T6 makes it.
findings.class_evidence: Six live mentions of Implementation Log are deliberate back-compat and must NOT be flagged (CHANGELOG.md:859, README.md:192, commands/summary.md:7, commands/summary.md:34, skills/hackify/SKILL.md:224, work-doc-template.md:5). C6 discriminates because those name the legacy label, they do not instruct a writer to write into it.

findings.refuter_verdict_verbatim: UPHELD, and this sprint manufactured the live half
findings.one_line: Two live rules gate the same decision-table cell incompatibly: the refuter maps a both-lenses REFUTED Critical straight to push-back, while review-triage/SKILL.md:61 forbids a bare push-back on a Critical without escalation and user sign-off.
findings.why: Falsifying it means comparing what two policy sentences MEAN, and no count, citation, token, check-reference, vocabulary or presence check reads meaning.
findings.replay_note: Fixed at 1249914. phase-5-refute.md no longer exists at the derived_at commit and review-triage/SKILL.md:61 now states the refuter supplies evidence rather than deciding the row.

findings.one_line: 71-release-mechanism-pins.sh says orchestration.md's "4-5 reviewers" row is deliberately NOT pinned, and the literal is in fact banned in RR_BANS at 77-reviewer-roster.sh:216.
findings.why: The sentence claims a quoted phrase is not pinned while that exact phrase is present in a ban list, which is C7's shape, and C7 is repo-wide so the scope refutation does not block the class.
findings.replay_note: Live at the derived_at commit. Re-routed to Phase 6 by the round 5 refuter, so it was carried out of the sprint unfixed and can be scored against the tree as it stands.
findings.class_evidence: At the derived_at commit the comment reads: orchestration.md's "4-5 reviewers" row is deliberately NOT pinned. The literal and the NOT pinned claim sit on ONE physical line, which is what makes the quoted phrase extractable by a line-based scan.
findings.reachability_caveat: Reachability depends on that line wrap holding. This tree hard-wraps at about 80 columns, and M2 in this same corpus is the finding that line-based matching goes blind on wrapped text. If the claim and its quoted literal ever land on separate lines, a line-based C7 loses it.

findings.one_line: CHANGELOG.md credited the GIF regeneration entirely to the Phase 3 caption and said nothing about the 40% size cut, so an accepted two-part fix reached the release notes as one part.
findings.why: It is a completeness gap between a release note and a decision accepted in prose elsewhere, and no class reads what a sentence FAILS to mention.
findings.replay_note: Fixed at 7b641e0. The GIF bullet at the derived_at commit now carries the 226,856 to 135,296 byte cut.

findings.one_line: Three files were said to be delivered and counted but never declared in the work-doc, and two of the three were in fact recorded there by DESCRIPTION rather than by filename.
findings.why: The finding was the parent's own false-clean filename grep, so a check that reported it would have to reproduce that same false negative, which makes claiming it a defect rather than a point.
findings.replay_note: Records-completeness question, not a textual claim. The genuinely unrecorded residue, scripts/validate-dod.d/75-ship-bar.sh, was recorded in the archived doc afterwards.
findings.class_evidence: A filename grep cannot match a description-based record. The work-doc named those files as "the two Phase 5 reviewer templates + mirrors" and "4 files not 2". The archived doc records this shape recurring at :806-809, :1119 and :1708.

findings.one_line: The throwaway test fixtures set repo-local git config but inherit global and system config, so a maintainer's core.hooksPath, merge.ff or commit.gpgsign can break them, and the comment claiming the fixture's reach is bounded by the temp dir is untrue.
findings.why: Falsifying the boundedness claim means running git under a hostile config and watching where it reaches, which is process behaviour no text scan observes.
findings.replay_note: Fixed at 6495b2b. GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null are set at three sites in scripts/test_ban_tokens.d/15-wi-absent-cases.sh at the derived_at commit.

findings.refuter_verdict_verbatim: UPHELD, the polarity really did flip, for two of four literals
findings.one_line: git grep -F is line based, so a banned phrase split across a hard line break is invisible to both scan halves, and as an absence pin that failure is silent rather than loud.
findings.why: It is a blind spot in how the scanner itself matches text, not a claim written in any file, so there is nothing for a claim check to read.
findings.replay_note: Declined as a fix, carried out of the sprint as backlog. FIX-H3 option C was measured and rejected because the whitespace-normalised screen would have added a fail-open inside a fail-closed check.

findings.one_line: agents/wave-implementer.md used {{test_file_path}} in its prompt body while declaring it in no INPUTS list and in no dispatch-table row.
findings.why: It is the C3 definition with nothing left over, a mustache token used in an agent prompt and absent from that prompt's INPUTS list, and C3 is repo-wide.
findings.replay_note: Fixed at ab5cb74. The string test_file_path returns zero hits across all tracked files at the derived_at commit, so this finding CANNOT be scored by running the check over the tree as it stands. It needs the historical blob or a fixture. This is the clearest case for T1b's fixtures half.

findings.one_line: A CHANGELOG bullet named four sites for the Reviewer F inversion including the two mode skills, and {{task_file_index}} occurs zero times in quick/SKILL.md and yolo/SKILL.md.
findings.why: Under C7 widened to both polarities, the bullet asserts a phrase was carried into the two mode skills and it is not there. That is decidable by looking for the literal, with no annotation needed, which is what unblocked it: the C1 labelling failed on the missing annotation, not on the shape.
findings.replay_note: Introduced mid-sprint and fixed at 7b641e0, so it is NOT live at the sprint base 03e7a12. Its replay base is 7b641e0~1, where CHANGELOG.md:20 carries the four-site claim and {{task_file_index}} occurs zero times in skills/quick/SKILL.md and skills/yolo/SKILL.md. Fixtures are therefore per-finding, not one global base.
findings.polarity_note: Was labelled C1/out_of_class/scope_blocked at freeze, on the grounds that C7 ran one direction only. Decision #13-A widened C7 rather than stretching the label. Recorded as AC1b bucket change 1 in docs/work/2026-08-24-claim-integrity.md.

bucket_history.reason: frozen state, before any check existed
decision #13-A widened C7 to both polarities; the check moved first and the bucket followed. The banned direction is the reverse.

findings.one_line: README.md:254 says performance.md carries 95 stable IDs and 10 domains, and the measured figures are 96 and 11.
findings.why: The count is unannotated and pre-existing in a file the diff never opened, and C1 is diff-scoped and annotation-driven, so both halves of C1's precondition fail at once.
findings.replay_note: Live at the derived_at commit, README.md:254 still reads 95 stable IDs, 10 domains. Re-routed to Phase 6 unfixed, so the check staying silent on it is provable against the tree as it stands.

findings.one_line: parallel-agents/README.md:12 says the two rows in the second table and that table has three rows.
findings.why: Same blocker as M5, an unannotated pre-existing count in a file the diff never opened, so the diff-scoped annotated-count class cannot see it.
findings.replay_note: Live at the derived_at commit. Re-routed to Phase 6 unfixed.

findings.one_line: The work-doc called 227,491 bytes byte-for-byte the size of the shipped asset when the base blob was 226,856, off by 635.
findings.why: Blocked twice over, the count is unannotated and it lives under docs/work/, which every scan excludes on purpose as a frozen record of what was true at the time.
findings.replay_note: Corrected in the same commit that filed it. The archived doc no longer carries the 227,491 claim at that line.

counts_note: Every total here is a clean partition, each finding counted exactly once. I6 is filed under refuted_on_fact only, even though no_class_reaches is also true of it, because refuted_on_fact is the stronger statement: no class may claim it. The runner cross-checks these totals against the per-finding data, so a later bucket edit that does not update this block turns the runner red. That is deliberate, and it is what AC1b is asking for.

notes.title: The reachable count is 3 of 13, and a small number is the honest answer
notes.body: Three findings are reachable: I2 by C6, I4 by C7, M3 by C3. Ten are not. This was derived by walking each finding against the seven frozen class definitions, not by adopting the archived plan's figure. It happens to land inside the Phase 2.5 spec review's independently derived band of 1 to 3, which was reached against only four classes rather than seven. The original sprint plan's 8 of 13 came from classifying findings as mechanically checkable in the sense that some script could in principle catch them, which is a different question from whether THIS design reaches them.

notes.title: Unsettled: the archived plan says C7 reaches M4, and under C7 as frozen it does not
notes.body: Sprint Backlog task T5d in the live work-doc says C7 is the class that reaches I4 and M4. C7 as frozen in this file runs one direction only, a sentence claiming a phrase is absent, unpinned or not present where it is in fact present. M4 is the inverse, a sentence claiming a phrase is present where it is in fact absent. Labelled under C1 with a scope_blocked bucket rather than stretching C7 to cover both polarities. If the sprint later widens C7 to both directions, M4 becomes reachable and the reachable count goes to 4. That widening would be a change to the check, and moving M4's bucket to follow it costs a work-doc entry under AC1b.

notes.title: Four of the seven classes reach nothing in this corpus, including the two W2 is about to build
notes.body: C1, C2, C4 and C5 each score zero here. W2 builds C2 (citations) and C4 (check-exists), the two cheapest classes, and neither touches a single finding in this corpus. That is not an argument against building them, both are cheap and repo-wide and C4 is the class the archived retrospective explicitly asks for after the parent reported a check that does not exist. It IS a sizing fact: the score will not move when W2 lands, and nobody should read a flat score there as the check failing. Written down now so it is not discovered at T6.

notes.title: The corpus is not scoreable in full against the tree as it stands
notes.body: Only I4, M5 and M6 are live at the derived_at commit. Of the three must_catch findings, one (I4) is live, one (I2) has its filed site fixed but three same-class siblings live, and one (M3) is gone from the tree entirely, zero hits for the string test_file_path across all tracked files. So a check run over today's tree can prove at most 1 of the 3 directly. T1b's fixtures half exists for exactly this, and T6 needs a written procedure per finding before it scores, not after.

notes.title: A sibling hit is not the filed finding
notes.body: I2's filed site was implement-and-test.md:34, fixed at ab5cb74. The live sites are debug-when-stuck.md:19, debug-when-stuck.md:190 and README.md:416, which the archived record names as out-of-file siblings carried out of the sprint deliberately. They are the same class, not the same finding. Whoever scores I2 at T6 must state which of the two they are counting.

notes.title: Reporting I6 as caught is a defect, not a point
notes.body: I6 was REFUTED on fact: the parent searched three filenames, got zero, and concluded the files were undeclared, when the work-doc recorded two of them by description rather than by name. A check that flags I6 has reproduced that false-clean grep. The finding carries claiming_is_defect so the runner can call it out separately instead of burying it in a generic wrongly-claimed total.

notes.title: Refuted on scope is not the same as refuted on fact
notes.body: Four findings were REFUTED. I4, M5 and M6 went on scope, meaning the text was byte-identical at the sprint base and the rationale was untouched, so the diff had no business fixing them. All three remain TRUE statements about the tree, which is why a class may still reach them. Only I6 was refuted on fact, and that is the one no class may claim. Verified corpus is the wrong phrase for this set as a whole.

notes.title: I4's reachability rests on a line wrap
notes.body: C7 reaches I4 because the quoted literal and the NOT pinned claim sit on one physical line at the derived_at commit. This tree hard-wraps markdown and shell comments at about 80 columns, and M2 in this same corpus is the finding proving line-based matching goes blind on wrapped text. AC1 demands 100% of the reachable set, so this dependency is stated rather than assumed. If the wrap changes, I4 stops being reachable by a line-based C7 and the bucket needs revisiting under AC1b.

notes.title: AC1b bucket change 1: M4 moved, and the direction it moved in is the point
notes.body: C7 as frozen read: 'A sentence claiming a phrase is absent, unpinned or not present, where it is in fact present. Repo-wide.' Decision #13-A widened it to both polarities, so M4 (a CHANGELOG bullet claiming a token was carried into two files it never reached) is now reachable, and the reachable set goes from 3 to 4. The order matters and is the whole reason AC1b exists: the CHECK was widened first, by a user decision, and the label followed. Moving a label so an unchanged check scores better is the banned move. M4 also does not replay at the sprint base, since it was born and died inside the sprint; its base is 7b641e0~1.
